Refuse short comment openers in the disclosure D-4 reader (#283)

TODO 255 records that the disclosure case with '<!-->' in
tools/test-build-site.py pins Python 3.14.4's HTMLParser reading of
that opener and fails under Python 3.14.7 in a side-by-side test.

Add SHORT_COMMENT, re.compile(r"<!---?>"), the same pattern as check 9
of tools/check-inline-code.py, and the exception ShortCommentRefused.
Before parsing, disclosure_d4_section() searches the whole text with
SHORT_COMMENT and, on a match, raises ShortCommentRefused, so on a text
with a match the result of disclosure_d4_section() does not come from
the interpreter's HTMLParser; disclosure_d4_section() still parses every
other text with that parser. The refusal names the text found, '<!-->'
or '<!--->', without calling that text a comment. In
check_disclosure_states(), d4_failures() gets 1 except clause around the
call of its reader, for ShortCommentRefused, which d4_failures() reports
as a failure line; check_disclosure_states() has no except clause around
its calls of d4_failures() with disclosure_d4_section(). A new case
checks that catch for 2 exception classes only: it passes d4_failures()
a stand-in reader that raises, whose ShortCommentRefused must become the
failure line and whose ValueError must pass out of d4_failures()
unchanged. check_disclosure_states() catches that planted ValueError
itself, so the case does not check that check_disclosure_states() lets
such an exception pass. The '<!-->' case now expects the refusal, and a
new '<!--->' case expects it too. A new '<!---->' case puts an Entry 5
label after the empty comment and the note after the label, and expects
no refusal and the lacks-note failure. The case does not show that the
reader parses '<!---->' as a comment, as the reader records only where
start tags stand. The '<!-->' case is a fixture brought up to date with
a deliberate contract change: the test's reader now refuses that opener.

The comment on SHORT_COMMENT and the docstring of
disclosure_d4_section() say that, before parsing,
disclosure_d4_section() searches the whole text with SHORT_COMMENT and
raises ShortCommentRefused on a match, and cite TODO 255's record of a
case that pins Python 3.14.4's reading of '<!-->' and fails under Python
3.14.7; the comment adds that TODO 255 records nothing about '<!--->'.
Check 9 of tools/check-inline-code.py searches with the same pattern;
check 9's message now names the text found, as "the text '<!-->' in an
HTML page", in place of "a comment that opens as '<!-->'". Check 9's
docstring entry says that check 9 refuses that text wherever it stands,
such as inside an attribute value. The docstring of markup_problems(),
which runs check 7's refusal of elements by name and checks 8 and 9, now
says what it refuses: each such element and each '<![CDATA[', both found
ignoring case, and each text '<!-->' or '<!--->', found by text matches
and not by the parser, wherever it stands, in place of calling them
markup that the parser reads differently from a browser. It also says
that check 7's rule on the light and dark switch runs in
switch_problems(). What checks 7 to 9 refuse is unchanged. A new case in
tools/test-inline-code.py puts '<!-->' in an attribute value and
requires check 9's new message.

Add .github/squash/283.txt, which holds this message byte for byte.
.python-version is unchanged.

Residual: this change adds a refusal of '<!-->' and '<!--->' to 1 reader
only, disclosure_d4_section(), which reads with the class Reader. This
change leaves unchanged the 11 other classes that the third check below
lists with Reader, each with HTMLParser as the only base in its class
statement. collect_document_tags() of tools/web_metadata.py feeds its
input straight to an instance of _DocumentTags, and ld_json_blocks() of
tools/check-page-metadata.py feeds its input straight to an instance of
_LDJSONScripts; neither function searches its input for these openers
first. So what each of the 2 functions collects from a text that holds
'<!-->' or '<!--->' depends on how the running interpreter's HTMLParser
reads that text. The fourth check feeds collect_document_tags() the text
'<!--><meta name=a><link rel=b>-->' and ld_json_blocks() the text
'<!--><script type=application/ld+json>{}</script>-->', and each
function the same text with '<!--->' and with '<!---->' in place of
'<!-->'. On Python 3.14.4, collect_document_tags() collects nothing from
its 2 texts that start with '<!-->' or '<!--->' and collects the meta
and the link element from its text that starts with '<!---->';
ld_json_blocks() collects nothing from its 2 texts that start with
'<!-->' or '<!--->' and collects the ld+json block from its text that
starts with '<!---->'. This message says nothing about what these 2
functions collect from any other input, which callers of the other 9
classes refuse these openers before those classes parse, or how Python
3.14.7 reads these openers in any of the 11 other classes.

Checks, from the repository root, with the outputs of Python 3.14.4:

- python3 -I tools/test-build-site.py prints
  "test-build-site: all 1125 cases passed." and exits 0.
- python3 -I tools/test-inline-code.py prints
  "test-inline-code: all 154 cases passed." and exits 0.
- This command exits 0 and prints 1 line per class in tools/*.py whose
  class statement has HTMLParser or html.parser.HTMLParser as the only
  base, the file and the class name:

  ```
  python3 -I -c "import pathlib, re; [print(path, name) for path in sorted(pathlib.Path('tools').glob('*.py')) for name in re.findall(r'class (\w+)\((?:html\.parser\.)?HTMLParser\)', path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))]"
  ```

  ```
  tools/build-site.py PageScan
  tools/check-inline-code.py InlineCodeParser
  tools/check-inline-code.py SwitchScan
  tools/check-install-page.py PageParser
  tools/check-install-page.py LoadScan
  tools/check-install-page.py TagReader
  tools/check-page-metadata.py _LDJSONScripts
  tools/check-release-checksum-live.py PageReader
  tools/check-release-links.py PageReader
  tools/test-build-site.py Placement
  tools/test-build-site.py Reader
  tools/web_metadata.py _DocumentTags
  ```

- This command exits 0 and prints 1 line per opener, the opener, then
  the meta and link elements collected and then the ld+json blocks
  collected:

  ```
  python3 -I -c "import runpy; m = runpy.run_path('tools/check-page-metadata.py'); [print(opener, m['web_metadata'].collect_document_tags(f'{opener}<meta name=a><link rel=b>-->'), m['ld_json_blocks'](f'{opener}<script type=application/ld+json>{{}}</script>-->')) for opener in ('<!-->', '<!--->', '<!---->')]"
  ```

  ```
  <!--> ([], []) []
  <!---> ([], []) []
  <!----> ([{'name': 'a'}], [{'rel': 'b'}]) ['{}']
  ```
